title: Opel workers stage 24-hour warning strike in Eisenach

tea.why: Workers rejected employer wage offers during collective bargaining in the metal and electrical industry.
tea.want: Union members demanded a 5 percent wage increase, profit sharing, and job and investment guarantees.
tea.changed: Nov 23: Opel staff in Eisenach initiated the first 24-hour warning strike in the plant's history.

summary: On 23 November 2026, employees at the Opel plant and nearby supplier companies in Eisenach began a 24-hour warning strike organized by the IG Metall union. Around 250 staff joined at the start on Monday morning, halting plant production entirely. The walkout formed part of sector-wide warning strikes across Germany ahead of regional collective bargaining talks in Mannheim. Protesters demanded a 5 percent pay increase over a 12-month period, worker profit-sharing, relief for lower pay grades, and binding commitments regarding site investments and job security. In response, the Thuringian metal and electrical industry employers association called the strike unnecessary, arguing that solutions must be reached at the negotiating table given high domestic production costs.
response: Matthias Kreft of the Association of the Metal and Electrical Industry in Thuringia stated the strike was unnecessary and that solutions must be reached through negotiations given high domestic costs.

crowd.text: around 250 workers according to MDR Thüringen

updates.text: Around 250 Opel and supplier employees in Eisenach started a 24-hour warning strike organized by IG Metall.
